Title: Boy, 11, dies after being shot with homemade gun in Keningau
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: An 11-year-old boy died from a gunshot wound to the head after being shot with a homemade firearm known as a 'Ginsok' in Kampung Mampulut, Sook, Keningau, last Saturday.
Keningau police chief Superintendent Erwansyah Abdul Basir said police received a report about the incident, which occurred at a rubber smallholding hut, at 2.35pm.
He said the victim was taken to Keningau Hospital but was pronounced dead.
"A post-mortem examination at Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Kota Kinabalu, yesterday confirmed the cause of death as a gunshot wound to the head.
"Preliminary investigations revealed that the victim was with another child in the smallholding hut before a single shot was fired," he said in a statement.
Erwansyah said the case was being investigated under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001 for negligence exposing a child to danger, and Section 8(a) of the Arms Act 1960 for possession of a firearm without a valid licence.
He said forensic and ballistic examinations were being conducted to determine how the homemade firearm was obtained, stored and handled.
Police were also investigating the weapon's firing mechanism, he added.
Erwansyah advised the public against possessing firearms without permission and reminded licensed firearm owners to keep their weapons in a safe and locked place.
He also urged the public to refrain from making statements that could interfere with the investigation.

Title: Malaysia should focus on tax revenue collection, not SST vs GST – Expert
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's tax debate should focus on enhancing revenue collection rather than choosing between the Sales and Service Tax (SST) and the Goods and Services Tax (GST), said an expert.
KPMG Malaysia senior advisor on tax policy Dr Veerinderjeet Singh said Malaysia already has the relevant taxes in place, with the key challenge being to ensure they perform effectively and deliver the intended revenue.
"I am not a proponent of introducing new types of taxes… we already have all the relevant types of taxes.
"Our challenge is to ensure that the taxes we have, whether income tax, SST or various duties, are performing effectively and generating the intended revenue, and extracting more revenue from the taxes we have," he said in a panel discussion titled "Post-Budget 2027 Debate", organised by the Malaysian Economic Association here today.
Veerinderjeet said the plans to incorporate elements of GST into the existing SST framework would be almost impossible, particularly due to the absence of a legal provision for an input-output tax mechanism.
While the government could explore ways to improve SST by adopting certain GST features, the two systems differed in key areas, including tax invoicing, input-output tax mechanisms and refunds, he said.
"We have already crossed the tax invoicing element. The e-invoicing system can effectively replace the tax invoice used under the GST system. The next issue is whether we have an input-output mechanism. That is the most difficult part, as there is no legal provision under SST legislation to allow for it.
"The third element is refunds. We do have certain refund mechanisms under the sales tax system, whereby eligible businesses can apply for refunds or drawbacks of duties if they meet specific objectives or conditions," he said.
Veerinderjeet said that Malaysia should strengthen the efficiency of its tax collection agencies, particularly the Inland Revenue Board (IRB) and the Customs Department, to maximise revenue from existing taxes.
He said the IRB had access to various tools, including data analytics, technology and data scientists, to improve tax collection, although questions remained over how effectively and efficiently these resources were being utilised.
-- BERNAMA

Title: Heavy rain triggers slope collapse, damages house in Kundasang
Article:
KUNDASANG: A slope collapse measuring about 25 metres high, triggered by continuous heavy rain, damaged the rear wall of a house in Kampung Pogun and Kampung Dumpiring Atas here yesterday.
No injuries or fatalities were reported, while another nearby house was found to be safe and undamaged.
The Civil Defence Force (APM), through the Kundasang Civil Defence Unit Centre (PUPA), deployed an officer and two personnel to monitor the site today.
APM said preliminary inspections found that the slope collapse was caused by continuous heavy rain in the area.
"As a safety measure, APM personnel and village residents installed a tarpaulin over the collapsed slope to prevent water from accumulating and reduce the risk of further soil erosion.
"Monitoring is also being carried out to ensure the safety of residents in the surrounding area," it said in a statement today.
APM advised residents, particularly those living on slopes and in high-risk areas, to remain alert for signs of ground movement.
Residents were also urged to follow safety instructions and move to a safer location immediately if they detected early signs of a landslide.
Continuous heavy rain since yesterday evening had also triggered landslides and flash floods in several areas around Kundasang.
These included an incident involving a Perodua Kancil, which was believed to have been swept away by strong currents before overturning on a roadside embankment in Kampung Sinisian.
District police chief Superintendent Mursalin Mahmud was reported as saying that another landslide occurred behind Surau Al-Taqwah in Kampung Dumpiring Bawah.
An overflow of water mixed with rocks also affected the main road connecting Kampung Pahu to Kampung Himbaan in Bundu Tuhan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pahang closes schools in Kuantan, Rompin as haze worsens
Article:
KUANTAN: Schools in Kuantan and Rompin will be closed tomorrow due to worsening haze, the Pahang Education Department said.
In a statement, the department said all educational institutions under its jurisdiction in the two districts would be temporarily closed from Oct 13, pending further instructions, following the haze and prevailing Air Pollutant Index (API) readings.
"During the closure, Home-Based Teaching and Learning (PdPR) will be conducted through suitable methods, taking into account students' capabilities, access and needs, as well as teachers' readiness.
"The reopening of schools will be announced through the department's official channels once conditions and API readings are deemed safe for operations to resume," it said in a statement.
The department said educational institutions in both districts had been instructed to minimise activities that could expose students and the education community to unhealthy air.
"Students, teachers and the education community are advised to take appropriate measures to safeguard their health, welfare and safety.
"Continuous monitoring will be carried out in collaboration with the Rompin and Kuantan district education offices and relevant agencies to ensure appropriate action is taken," it said.
The department also instructed all educational institutions in the two districts to monitor API readings continuously and comply with directives issued by the Education Ministry, Department of Environment and Health Ministry.
As of 5pm, two monitoring stations in Pahang had recorded unhealthy air quality, with Balok Baru in Kuantan registering an API reading of 162 and Rompin recording 155.
Last Friday, all educational institutions in Rompin were
temporarily closed
for a day due to worsening haze.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MN Holdings bags RM293.9 mln data centre infrastructure contract
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MN Holdings Bhd's wholly owned subsidiary MN Power Transmission Sdn Bhd has secured a total contract value of RM293.88 million for the construction of two 275 kilovolt (kV) consumer landing stations (CLSs) for a data centre development located in the central region of Peninsular Malaysia.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, the infrastructure utilities construction and engineering solutions specialist said it will undertake the construction, supply, installation, testing and commissioning of the CLS facilities,  including the main building works and related external works.
"The construction work commenced in September 2026, and is expected to be completed in August 2027," it said.
MN Holdings executive director Datuk Dang Siong Diang said the project demonstrates the continued demand for high-voltage power infrastructure to support large-scale data centre developments.
"Our experience in delivering high-voltage substations and power infrastructure positions us well to participate in this growing segment.
"We remain focused on executing these projects effectively while continuing to pursue opportunities across the power infrastructure, data centre and utilities sectors across Peninsular Malaysia," he said.

Title: Kedah teen held captive, tortured for two days before being killed
Article:
ALOR SETAR: An 18-year-old teen found dead in bushes near Jalan Harvard in Sungai Petani on Oct 8 was held captive for two days, tortured and had his hair cut before being beaten to death and dumped by the roadside.
Kedah police chief Datuk Adzli Abu Shah said police were alerted to the discovery of the dead body at 8.05am on Thursday.
He said the body was sent to the Sultanah Bahiyah Hospital forensic department for a post-mortem.
"The post-mortem found that the cause of death was blunt force trauma to the head
"Investigations also found that the incident arose from the main suspect's anger after residents complained that the victim had stolen a motorcycle," he said at a press conference.
Adzli said police arrested 14 men, aged between 16 and 24, in Gurun and Guar Chempedak between noon and 10.30pm on the same day.
He said police also seized 14 mobile phones of various brands, a silver Honda City, a pair of scissors and an identity card believed to belong to the victim.
Adzli said only one of the 14 suspects had a previous criminal record, involving a drug-related offence.
He said 12 suspects had been remanded for six days until Wednesday, while two underage suspects were remanded for five days until tomorrow to facilitate investigations.
"The victim, aged 18, was accused of stealing a motorcycle belonging to one of the suspects, although no police report had been lodged.
"The suspects took matters into their own hands, apprehending the victim in Pendang on Oct 5 and taking him to a house in Gurun, where he was held for two days.
"During those two days, the victim was beaten and tortured, and his hair was cut. He was eventually found dead on the night of Oct 7.
"They then dumped his body by the roadside the following day, before the public discovered the body at 8am," he said.
Adzli said the scissors seized by police were believed to have been used to cut the victim's hair, but the blunt object used in the assault had yet to be found.
He said investigations found that no police report had been lodged over the motorcycle theft.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
Section 302 of the Penal Code carries the death penalty or a jail term of between 30 and 40 years, and not fewer than 12 strokes of the rotan upon conviction.

Title: 2027 power subsidy plan under review: Treasury sec-gen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is reviewing the electricity subsidy mechanism for 2027 with Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) and the Energy Commission.
Implementation parameters and funding arrangements are yet to be finalised, according toTreasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican.
Johan said the current mechanism, which runs until Dec 31, aims to protect about 85 per cent of households from higher electricity bills.
He said the expansion of subsidy protection accounted for increased electricity consumption during hot weather and haze, which pushed some households beyond the previous monthly threshold of 600 kilowatt-hours (kWh).
This resulted in significantly higher electricity bills for affected consumers, prompting the government to review the level of protection.
"The government is reviewing the way forward with TNB and ST, including the parameters for next year and the extent to which the costs will be borne by the government or through the relevant adjustment mechanism," he said.
Johan was responding to a question at a post-2027 Budget debate today.
He said the decision on the electricity subsidy mechanism for next year had not been finalised, including how the costs would be shared between the government and TNB.
On Sept 17, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that the electricity bill protection threshold for domestic customers would be raised to 800kWh a month from 600kWh.
He said the move was an immediate measure to ease the burden on households facing higher electricity bills.
Under this measure, domestic customers consuming up to 800kWh a month will be exempt from the automatic fuel cost adjustment charge, the eight per cent sales and service charge and retail charges.

Title: Johor mosques, surau to hold solat hajat until haze improves
Article:
JOHOR BARU: All mosques and surau in Johor have been asked to hold special prayers after Maghrib today and continue doing so until the haze improves.
State Islamic Religious Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khalid said the solat hajat initiative was aimed at seeking divine intervention for the haze to subside and air quality to improve.
He urged Muslims across the state to take part in the prayers and seek protection for the public's health and well-being.
The initiative comes as seven of Johor's eight air quality monitoring stations recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, with Pasir Gudang recording the highest at 174.
Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) was the dominant pollutant at all eight stations, while Segamat was the only location with a moderate API reading.
Fared expressed hope that the collective prayers would contribute to the well-being of Johoreans as the state awaits an improvement in air quality.

Title: 100 students advance to final round of MRSM Bintang Media 2026 challenge
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 100 students from 42 Mara Junior Science Colleges (MRSM) nationwide advanced to the final round of MRSM Bintang Media 2026 held at Balai Berita, Bangsar, today.
MRSM Bintang Media 2026, held as part of the 'Siri Jelajah MRSM' and Media Prima Talent Development Programme, aimed to give students first-hand exposure to the media industry by learning directly from experienced media practitioners.
The programme featured four categories — Journalism and News Writing by Berita Harian (BH), The Art of Writing and News Journalism by New Straits Times (NST), Broadcasting and News Presentation, and Photojournalism and Visual Storytelling.
The finalists were selected from a pool of 678 students from 58 MRSM campuses nationwide. Online coaching sessions were held from Sept 8 to 11, covering all four categories.
Berita Harian Group Editor Zulkifli Jalil, in his welcoming remarks, called on participants to make full use of the opportunity and not be afraid to ask questions or make mistakes.
"You might be here today as participants, but one day, you may come back as journalists or editors," he said.
Muhammad Syahril Suhaimi, a teacher from MRSM Pendang, said the programme received an encouraging response from students.
"Many students have shown interest because this is different from their usual classroom activities. We can see new passions and talents emerging among them."
Evaldo Joey Edwin, a student of MRSM Kota Kinabalu, said that being at Balai Berita, Bangsar was a golden opportunity.
"I know it is not easy to get in here. I am very happy and grateful for the opportunity," he added.
Meanwhile, Muhammad Hazray Haikasya Mohd Haizam, 15, from MRSM Langkawi said he hoped to make the most of this opportunity to represent his college.
He said that although his ambition was to become a veterinarian, he remained open to other opportunities.
"This experience has allowed me to explore other fields, especially broadcasting and the media industry," he said.
[[nid:1553884]]
Prior to the final round, participants underwent coaching sessions conducted by journalists, photographers and editors from New Straits Times Press (NSTP), covering areas including news writing, reporting, presentation, photography and visual storytelling.
The final round began at 3pm today, with participants given until 5pm to complete and submit their work in their respective categories.
The closing ceremony will be held tomorrow, where the winners of the competition are scheduled to be announced in the presence of Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) chairman, Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.
Media Prima News and Current Affairs Convergence Operations Editor-in-Chief M Thillinadan, New Straits Times Press circulation general manager Prakash Munusamy, Assistant Director (Innovation and Research), Mara's Secondary Education Division, Muhamad Hazmil Ismail were also present during the opening ceremony.

Title: Budget must fire up corporate growth: CGS International CEO
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Corporate Malaysia should leverage the 2027 Budget to accelerate investment, improve productivity and build more sustainable and internationally competitive businesses amid rising global uncertainties.
CGS International Securities Malaysia Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Khairi Shahrin Arief Baki said the fifth Madani Budget offered businesses opportunities to strengthen resilience through technology adoption, workforce development, sustainability and increased productive capacity.
Khairi said escalating geopolitical tensions in West Asia, disruptions to energy and shipping, trade tensions and climate risks had made resilience a priority for Malaysia and its corporate sector.
"The budget gives businesses more tools to invest in technology, skills, sustainability and productive capacity before the next test arrives.
"The government can set the conditions, clear the barriers and lay the foundations. Whether those foundations translate into stronger businesses, better jobs and higher incomes is ultimately up to companies," he said.
CGS International said among the measures supporting corporate transformation are the extension of accelerated capital allowances for locally produced plant and machinery, information and communications technology equipment and software until the end of 2030.
The budget also provides investment tax allowances of up to 100 per cent for qualifying green technology projects and assets, alongside support for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) adopting artificial intelligence and automation.
He said the proposed increase in the minimum wage from RM1,700 to RM2,000 a month from June 2027, with exemptions for MSMEs recording annual sales below RM50 million, is expected to reinforce the need for businesses to move towards higher-productivity operations.
"Productivity without better wages leaves households outside the gains of growth. Wages without productivity cannot hold. Malaysia needs both, rising together," he said.
On sustainability, Khairi said companies that invested early in decarbonisation and operational efficiency would be better positioned to manage the costs and implications of the country's evolving carbon-pricing framework.
"Carbon pricing is becoming part of Malaysia's business landscape. Companies can treat it as a compliance issue, or as a reason to become more efficient and more resilient. Sustainability done well can be a source of productivity, resilience and long-term value," he said.
Khairi also highlighted how the MY Value Up Programme, introduced by the Securities Commission and Bursa Malaysia in 2026, could reinforce that shift.
It encourages listed companies to set out clearer growth strategies, targets and capital-allocation priorities, and targeted companies are expected to begin publishing their MY Value Up plans in 2027.
"The 2027 Budget supplies many of the enabling conditions for transformation. MY Value Up can help listed companies turn them into clear strategies, disciplined capital allocation and value that can be measured," he added.

Title: Lee Lam Thye: Workplace sustainability must put workers' safety, health first
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Workplace sustainability must prioritise workers' safety, health and dignity, with stronger governance and accountability needed to prevent accidents and protect lives, said Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye.
"There can be no truly sustainable workplace without sustainable people," said the Pertubuhan Ikatan Komuniti Selamat (Ikatan) chairman in a speech at Universiti Sains Malaysia's (USM) seminar on Building Safer and Healthier Workplaces.
Lee said workplace sustainability must go beyond environmental protection, energy conservation and technological advancement to include physical safety, mental well-being and work environments designed around human needs.
He said organisations could not claim to be sustainable if workers were exposed to excessive stress, fatigue, workplace injuries or poorly designed systems in the pursuit of productivity.
Speaking on governance in occupational safety and health (OSH) systems and workplace sustainability, Lee called for a shift from mere regulatory compliance to a strong culture of prevention, accountability and continuous improvement.
He said safety must be embedded in leadership, business decisions and corporate culture, rather than treated as an administrative requirement or the sole responsibility of safety officers.
"A safe workplace begins with good governance, and good governance begins with leadership and accountability," he said.
Lee urged employers and senior management to establish clear safety policies, allocate adequate resources, conduct effective risk assessments and regularly monitor workplace safety performance.
Workers closest to workplace hazards often understood the risks better than anyone else, he said, adding that those who raised safety concerns should be regarded as safety partners rather than troublemakers.
Lee further called on organisations to investigate accidents by examining systemic failures instead of simply blaming individuals.
"Investigations should assess factors such as inadequate training, unsuitable equipment, fatigue, unclear instructions, poor supervision and production pressures to prevent similar incidents from recurring.
"Greater use of preventive indicators, including hazard reports, ergonomic assessments, safety inspections, training effectiveness and psychosocial risk assessments is needed, rather than relying solely on accident statistics," he added.
Lee identified five pillars of effective safety governance which are leadership, human-centred design, worker participation, data-driven learning and continuous improvement.
He also warned that unethical and corrupt practices could undermine workplace safety, citing substandard protective equipment, falsified records, circumvention of standard operating procedures and conflicts of interest in awarding contracts.
"Integrity, transparency and accountability are essential to ensuring workers received adequate protection and organisations fulfilled their responsibilities," he said.
Referring to Malaysia's Occupational Safety and Health Act 1994, as amended, Lee said legal compliance was important but organisations must go further by identifying risks early and strengthening preventive measures.
As workplaces increasingly adopt artificial intelligence, automation and digitalisation, he said, technology must serve people rather than compromise their well-being.
"The future of workplace safety cannot simply be about preventing accidents. It must be about designing workplaces where people can work safely, remain healthy, maintain their dignity and continue contributing throughout their working lives," he said.
Lee added that sustainable workplaces required a human-centred approach that placed workers' welfare at the heart of organisational decision-making.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Minimum-wage exemption apt for MSMEs to ease cost pressure: Samenta
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Exempting micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) from the RM2,000 minimum wage requirement is necessary to ease cost pressures and preserve their capacity to invest, automate and expand.
Small and Medium Enterprises Association of Malaysia (Samenta) president Datuk William Ng said businesses had faced mounting cost pressures over the past two years, even before the latest energy crisis, squeezing profit margins despite higher sales.
"You may have nice gross domestic product numbers, you may have SMEs reporting higher sales figures.
"But when it comes to the bottom line, things are not looking very good," he said during a panel session at a post-2027 debate today.
Ng said the association supported the government's decision to exempt MSMEs from the latest minimum wage increase, as higher labour costs could further strain businesses already facing tight margins.
He said the concern was not widespread business closures, but the potential loss of funds SMEs needed for productivity improvements and expansion.
"Our fear was that if you impose a higher wage at a time when there is severe marginal compression, you wipe out whatever spare or extra income that the SME has that are supposedly earmarked for automation, for buying new machinery, for growth," he said.
He added that the funds were also needed for compliance with new environmental, social and governance (ESG) requirements, the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism and other obligations.
Ng said many SMEs in the Klang Valley already paid wages above RM2,000, but the impact could differ for smaller businesses in other parts of the country.
He cited a small food stall operator in Kota Bharu who employed a neighbour with limited education and skills, saying an additional RM300 in monthly wages could determine whether the worker retained his job.
"That RM300 extra that it comes through would have made a difference in whether I might still hire this neighbour, because I don't really need him.
"I just want to help out so that, you know, he gets some income," he added.
Ng said some businesses might respond to higher labour costs by reducing hiring or passing additional costs to consumers, rather than shutting down.
He also acknowledged concerns that the exemption could create a two-tier minimum wage system, with workers at larger companies receiving higher minimum pay than those employed by smaller businesses.
"Of course, the fact that now you have got two tiers of minimum wage doesn't help because we do want to equalise that eventually. But it is what it is," he said.
Ng said SMEs employed about half of the country's workforce, while workers in smaller businesses generally had lower education and skill levels than those employed by government-linked companies and multinational corporations.
For these workers, he said, retaining employment was also an important consideration alongside efforts to improve wages.
"Of course minimum wage is important, but the job itself is even more important," added Ng.
When tabling the 2027 Budget last Friday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that loan facilities and financing guarantees for MSMEs would increase to RM57 billion in 2027, up from RM50 billion.
He also announced a one-percentage-point reduction in corporate income tax rates for MSMEs.
The minimum wage will rise from RM1,700 to RM2,000 effective June 2027.
MSMEs recording annual sales below RM50 million are exempted from implementing the revised rate to give them time to adjust their business models.

Title: Teacher accused of forcing pupils to perform oral sex during home tuition
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A teacher has been accused of sexually abusing several male pupils, including forcing them to perform oral sex during tuition classes at his home in Bukit Jalil over the past few months.
The teacher, who works at a school in Bukit Jalil, held tuition classes at his residence for pupils, including those attending the school where he teaches.
A source said several parents lodged police reports yesterday after learning about the incidents.
"Several 11-year-old boys were sent by their parents to the teacher's home for tuition classes.
"The incidents had been occurring for several months, and some of the victims also attended the school where the teacher works," the source said.
The source said most of the pupils claimed they had been forced to perform oral sex, while some were nearly subjected to other forms of sexual assault.
"The school authorities are also believed to be aware of the alleged misconduct, and an internal investigation is underway," the source added.
Harian Metro is seeking confirmation from the police on the incident.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'We feel threatened until he is punished,' says stabbed nurse's daughter
Article:
KOTA BARU: The daughter of a nurse who was stabbed by her husband attended the Sessions Court here today to follow proceedings involving her stepfather, whom she believes is not mentally ill.
Nik Ruziany Nik Ahmad Ruzi, 19, said she was determined to be present to hear the charges against her 44-year-old stepfather, whom she described as cruel for stabbing her mother.
"Today I am here with several family members, although my heart hurts to see my stepfather, who treated my mother in a way that left her hospitalised.
"I accept the court's decision to send him to Hospital Bahagia in Perak for mental treatment, but as a stepdaughter, I am sure he is not mentally ill.
"What I can say is that the man's actions have traumatised our whole family, including my grandmother, who was also injured in last Monday's incident," she said when met at the court.
She said the family would not feel safe until her stepfather was given an appropriate sentence.
"I pray that he receives a sentence that matches his actions. We will continue to feel threatened until he is punished.
"We siblings have become numb, because every time they fought, my stepfather often threatened to kill my mother, and we also have evidence," she said.
Earlier, the unemployed man was charged in the Sessions Court with stabbing his wife with a knife and injuring his mother-in-law at a house in Padang Lepai, Ketereh, last Monday.
Shahrul Shahrizal Che Shaari, 44, pleaded not guilty and claimed trial after the charges were read to him separately before judges Zulkifli Ablah and Nik Habri Muhamad.
On Monday, the nurse was
critically injured after being stabbed six times
by her husband at their home in Kampung Padang Lepai, near Kadok.
The victim, 44, sustained serious stab wounds to her body and neck and is receiving treatment at Raja Perempuan Zainab II Hospital.

Title: Opposition proposes renaming Putrajaya Hospital after Dr Siti Hasmah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Opposition leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin has backed a proposal to rename Putrajaya Hospital after the late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali in recognition of her contributions to the country's healthcare system.
He said Perikatan Nasional would pursue the proposal if it came to power and the current government had not implemented it.
"We can propose it. If the government doesn't do it, we'll do it next time," he said when debating the 2027 Budget at the policy stage in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Hamzah (PN-Larut) was responding to a proposal by Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin (PN-Masjid Tanah) to name the hospital after the wife of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad.
Mas Ermieyati said the move would be a fitting tribute to Dr Siti Hasmah.
Dr Siti Hasmah died at 100-years-old at the
National Heart Institute
on Sept 28 and was laid to rest at the Presint 20 Muslim Cemetery, Putrajaya.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Viral image of crocodile near Seberang Jaya Hospital being probed
Article:
SEBERANG JAYA: An image purportedly showing a crocodile in a drain outside Seberang Jaya Hospital has gone viral, prompting calls for an investigation into its authenticity.
Seberang Jaya assemblyman Izhar Shah Arif Shah said he had alerted the Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) and the Drainage and Irrigation Department (DID) after receiving the information.
"At the same time, some concerned individuals have helped check whether the image is genuine or generated by artificial intelligence (AI).
"Genuine or otherwise, I have brought the matter to the attention of both agencies and proposed an investigation to establish the facts and determine the appropriate action.
"Either way, public safety remains a priority," he said in a Facebook post.
The authenticity of the image has yet to be established.
The New Straits Times has reached out to the state Perhilitan office for comments.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: IJM Corporation bags RM1.23 bln contruction contract for AT&S facilities in Kedah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: IJM Corporation Bhd's wholly-owned subsidiary, IJM Construction Sdn Bhd, has accepted a letter of award from AT&S Austria Technologie & Systemtechnik (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd for a design and build contract worth about RM1.23 billion.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the contract involves the construction of a four-storey production facility, a three-storey central utility building and a single-storey wastewater treatment facility at Kulim Hi-Tech Park, Kedah.
"The project is scheduled to commence in the fourth quarter of 2026 and is expected to be completed within 14 months from the commencement date," it said.
IJM Corporation added that the project is expected to contribute positively to the revenue and earnings of the group starting from the financial year ending 2027.

Title: Iswami calls for stronger regional action on haze
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Ikatan Setiakawan Wartawan Malaysia-Indonesia (Iswami) Malaysia has called for stronger regional cooperation to address transboundary haze caused by forest and land fires in Indonesia.
Its acting president Datuk Ahmad Zaini Kamaruzzaman said stronger Asean commitments were needed in prevention, preparedness and emergency response to realise the region's goal of becoming haze-free.
He said Iswami Malaysia had outlined five priorities, including protecting public health through air quality monitoring, accurate information, health advice and protective measures for vulnerable groups.
"Indonesia should strengthen fire prevention and enforcement by intensifying firefighting efforts, preventing open burning and taking firm action against those who violated the law," he said in a statement.
Zaini called for Malaysia and Indonesia to share hotspot data, smoke movement monitoring, information and technical assistance, and coordinate firefighting operations when necessary.
He urged journalists to report accurately and responsibly, prioritising facts, expert views and the experiences of affected communities while avoiding narratives that blamed an entire country's population.
"Transboundary haze should no longer be treated as a seasonal problem without effective, measurable long-term solutions," he said.
"Iswami believes sincere cooperation, clear accountability and effective action were essential to prevent recurring haze from continuing to affect people's lives and environmental sustainability," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Immigration Dept to intensify crackdown on illegal foreign workers, employers in Janda Baik
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department will intensify enforcement operations in Janda Baik, Pahang, following concerns raised by residents over the growing presence of foreigners and their involvement in economic activities in the area.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the department was taking the concerns seriously, particularly over the possibility of illegal employment and accommodation arrangements involving undocumented foreigners.
He said enforcement efforts would not only target undocumented migrants but also employers, business operators and property owners found employing, harbouring or allowing them to stay on their premises.
"The Immigration Department takes seriously the concerns raised by residents regarding the presence and involvement of foreigners in economic activities around Janda Baik, Bentong, as reported by the media on Oct 11.
"We will continue strengthening intelligence-led enforcement, focusing not only on undocumented migrants but also employers, premises owners and operators, as well as any parties employing, harbouring or allowing undocumented foreigners to reside on premises under their control," he said in a statement.
Zakaria revealed that the Pahang Immigration Department had previously conducted an enforcement operation in Janda Baik on April 24, during which eight locations were inspected.
A total of 82 individuals were screened during the operation, resulting in the detention of 38 foreigners suspected of committing various immigration offences.
He said the department would step up surveillance, intelligence gathering and enforcement operations based on information and complaints received from the public.
Zakaria acknowledged that the presence of foreigners in Janda Baik was partly driven by employment opportunities and economic activities, particularly in the tourism sector.
These included resorts, chalets and other accommodation establishments, as well as agricultural and commercial activities.
However, he warned that such economic opportunities could also create avenues for the illegal employment of foreigners and the provision of accommodation arrangements that violated immigration laws.
He said employers and premises owners found breaching immigration regulations could face legal action under the Immigration Act 1959/63, including Sections 55B and 55E, where applicable.
Zakaria said the department would also strengthen cooperation with local authorities and other enforcement agencies to address the issue comprehensively.
This would involve intelligence sharing and coordinated enforcement action within the respective jurisdictions of the agencies involved.
He said cooperation from residents and local community associations was equally important in identifying suspected immigration violations.
"The department appreciates the cooperation of local residents and residents' associations in providing information on activities suspected of violating immigration laws.
"Accurate information will enable us to verify complaints and take appropriate action without requiring members of the public to expose themselves to unnecessary risks," he said.
Zakaria assured residents that the department would continue monitoring developments in Janda Baik and ensure sustained enforcement action against immigration offences.
He said appropriate action would be taken against any party found violating immigration laws.

Title: Tok Mat: Malaysians advised to postpone Umrah trips amid security concerns
Article:
SEPANG: Malaysians are advised to temporarily postpone travel to Saudi Arabia for umrah following security concerns after a deadly attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said.
He said that while there had been no incident in Makkah, the missile attack in Riyadh had prompted the government to advise Malaysians to defer non-essential travel to Makkah and Madinah for the time being.
"There has been no incident in Makkah, but the missile explosion in Riyadh has raised security concerns," he told reporters after attending the departure of Jordan's King Abdullah II at the Bunga Raya Complex here.
Yesterday, the Foreign Ministry reported that no Malaysians had been killed or injured in Saturday's attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh or the incident involving a projectile that fell near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.
Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation reported that the attack on King Khalid International Airport killed 12 people and injured 309 others.
The fatalities comprised four Saudi nationals, two Bangladeshis and one national each from the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan.

Title: Growth must lift living standards: Johan Merican
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's strong economic performance must translate into tangible improvements in living standards as the government balances economic growth with fiscal consolidation under the 2027 Budget.
Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Merican said Malaysia had recorded encouraging economic growth, but the gains had yet to fully translate into public satisfaction with the economy.
"The budget remains anchored on the Ekonomi Madani framework, with greater emphasis on an inclusive approach to ensure that the needs of various segments of society including the B40, M40 and T20 groups, as well as the young and elderly continue to be addressed," he said at a post-budget discussion, today.
Malaysia's economy grew 5.2 per cent in 2025, while the government has projected growth of between 4.8 and 5.3 per cent this year, before moderating to between 4.2 and 5.2 per cent in 2027.
Johan said addressing the cost of living remained a priority, noting that household incomes had not increased in line with rising living costs despite inflation remaining under control.
"In a context where inflation in Malaysia is under control, one of the sources of the cost-of-living challenge is that income levels have not increased in line with the rising cost of living," he said.
He added that increasing incomes was therefore important, with the minimum wage serving as one of the measures to address the issue, although it would not resolve the challenge on its own.
The minimum wage is set to increase from RM1,700 to RM2,000 in June next year, with the government giving larger companies time to adjust their wage structures before extending the implementation to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
"The hope is that these large companies will also look at their overall salary structures and make adjustments based on the increase in the minimum wage," he said.
Johan said the government had also set a living-wage benchmark of RM3,400 for government-linked companies (GLCs), which could serve as a reference for private-sector employers in determining salaries.
He added that the government wanted employers to consider wages across different employee groups.
This includes starting salaries for graduates and diploma holders, rather than focusing solely on the lowest-paid workers.
On concerns about the impact of higher minimum wages on businesses, Johan said the RM2,000 rate had been presented to and approved by the National Wages Consultative Council, which includes representatives from both employers and workers.
He said the rate itself had not been disputed in the council's deliberations, while the Cabinet had considered allowing MSMEs more time to implement the increase.
"We are starting with large companies first because we also understand that MSMEs are among those affected by the conflict in Middle East and may need more time to adjust their business models," he said.
On fiscal policy, Johan said the government would continue reducing its deficit gradually while maintaining sufficient spending to support economic activity amid global uncertainty.
He said maintaining investor confidence through disciplined and prudent financial management remained a priority as the government pursued its fiscal consolidation targets.
"One key priority is to maintain investor confidence by demonstrating that Malaysia can implement disciplined and prudent financial management," he said.
Johan said the fiscal deficit narrowed to 3.7 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2025, with the government projecting 3.6 per cent this year, slightly above its original target of 3.5 per cent.
The government aims to reduce the deficit to 3.3 per cent in 2027 and three per cent by 2028 under the Fiscal Responsibility Act.
He said the national debt ratio was projected to decline from 65.2 per cent in 2025 to about 64 per cent this year and 63.7 per cent in 2027.
However, he noted that the government had factored in the possibility of oil prices remaining elevated amid uncertainty in the Middle East.
Petroleum product subsidies are estimated at about RM40 billion this year, with the government projecting a similar amount for 2027.
He said the government would adjust its approach if oil prices exceeded expectations, as it had done this year.
"If oil prices are higher than expected, we will make adjustments according to the circumstances," he said.
Johan said the 2027 Budget allocates RM459.8 billion for operating and development expenditure, up from RM419.2 billion under the 2026 Budget.
Including investments by GLCs, statutory bodies and public-private partnerships, the total would reach about RM510 billion, up from RM470 billion.

Title: Zaliha proposes gender-responsive budget statement
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Finance Ministry should prepare a Gender Responsive Budget Statement detailing how public spending benefits women and identifying gaps in policies affecting them, said Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa.
Zaliha, who is Government Backbenchers Club (BBC) chairman, said the statement should detail allocations, beneficiary groups, targets and policy outcomes by gender, beginning with the Women, Family and Community Development Ministry before being extended to other ministries.
Gender-responsive budgeting takes into account the different needs of women and men to ensure public resources are allocated fairly.
"I would like to propose that the Finance Ministry consider preparing a Gender Responsive Budget Statement detailing allocations, beneficiary groups, targets and policy outcomes according to gender.
"In my view, these perspectives deserve to be heard, given due consideration and taken into account in efforts to improve the effectiveness of government policies," she said in the Dewan Rakyat.
Zaliha said allocations benefiting women were spread across ministries, as policies on transport, employment, health, education and housing affected their safety, economic participation and well-being.
She said this step would help the government assess who benefited from public spending and identify gaps.
The call came amid concerns raised by non-governmental organisations over women's economic participation, unpaid care work and protection services for victims of gender-based violence.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Banks ease loan repayment concerns for families of missing Malaysians
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Banks have given interim assurances that they will not pressure families of 54 Malaysians missing after floods in Nepal, Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope said.
Its coordinator and spokesperson, Dr R. Manivannan, said the assurance followed a two-and-a-half-hour meeting at Bank Negara Malaysia involving financial institutions, insurance companies and the missing Malaysians' next of kin.
"Banks have assured the families that they will not pursue loan repayments or other payments until an agreement is reached," he said.
Dr Manivannan said Masfih welcomed the commitment but was awaiting a written framework from Bank Negara setting out measures to protect the families from further financial hardship.
He said the families needed a clear, coordinated solution to their loved ones' outstanding financial commitments.
"We have stopped the bleeding but not treated the injuries," he said.
In a separate statement, Bank Negara said the meeting involved 44 next of kin and representatives from financial institutions and financial service providers.
It said the discussions aimed to better understand the challenges families faced in managing the victims' financial affairs and to work towards appropriate and reasonable solutions.
"Bank Negara and the financial industry representatives also reiterated readiness to extend appropriate relief and support to the families of the victims affected by this tragedy, in accordance with applicable laws and regulatory requirements," the central bank said.
Bank Negara said the meeting also agreed that financial service providers would assign dedicated contact persons to reach out to the respective families and help them navigate administrative processes.
Dr Manivannan said Masfih had submitted a 35-page proposal to Bank Negara outlining relief measures, including a mechanism to address outstanding loans, credit commitments and liabilities while the missing people's status remained unresolved.
He said Bank Negara had appointed four officers to liaise with the families.
The officers would serve as points of contact, reducing the need for families to repeatedly explain their circumstances to different banks, insurers and agencies.
Masfih had also requested an additional officer who speaks Tamil and understands the case to improve communication with affected families, Dr Manivannan said.
"We have asked for one more officer who is Tamil-speaking and understands the matter so that communication with the affected families can be clearer and more effective," he said.
He said the arrangement would also help protect families from scam calls seeking personal or financial information.
"We want to ensure that they do not fall victim to scam calls or provide sensitive information to people who claim to represent the authorities or financial institutions," he said.
A mountain and glacier collapse near Nepal's border with China triggered catastrophic flooding in the Himalayas on Aug 26.
More than 1,400 people were killed and over 5,000 remain missing after tsunami-like waves swept through northern mountainous areas, destroying homes, roads, bridges and settlements.
Dr Manivannan said the interim assurances were a positive first step but should not replace a formal policy covering the families' financial concerns.
Masfih also wanted an urgent meeting with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to facilitate a coordinated government response and secure clear assurances on the way forward.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rain fails to clear Johor haze as seven areas record unhealthy air
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Rainfall has failed to bring widespread relief from the haze in Johor, with seven of the state's eight air quality monitoring stations recording unhealthy readings today.
The latest Air Pollutant Index (API) readings showed Pasir Gudang recording the highest level at 174, followed by Kota Tinggi (170) and Pengerang (166).
Larkin recorded an API reading of 159, Batu Pahat 156, Tangkak 152 and Kluang 144, all within the unhealthy range of 101 to 200.
Segamat was the only district to record moderate air quality, with an API reading of 95.
Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) was the dominant pollutant at all eight monitoring stations.
Residents are advised to limit prolonged outdoor activities, particularly strenuous exercise, and reduce their exposure to polluted air.

Title: Bank Negara, financial industry ready to support Nepal victims' families
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia and financial institutions are ready to provide relief and support to families of Malaysians missing after the Nepal-China floods, subject to applicable laws and regulatory requirements.
"Bank Negara and the financial industry representatives reiterated readiness to extend appropriate relief and support to the families of the victims affected by this tragedy, in accordance with applicable laws and regulatory requirements," Bank Negara said in a statement.
The meeting involved 44 next of kin and representatives from financial industry associations and financial service providers.
It aimed to better understand the issues and challenges families faced in handling the victims' financial affairs and work towards appropriate and reasonable solutions.
Bank Negara also expressed its deepest sympathies to the families affected by the tragedy.
The meeting agreed that financial service providers would assign dedicated contact persons to reach out to the respective families and help them navigate the required administrative processes.
The financial industry representatives included the Association of Banks in Malaysia, the Association of Islamic Banking and Financial Institutions Malaysia, Persatuan Insurans Am Malaysia, the Life Insurance Association of Malaysia and the Malaysian Takaful Association.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Schools in Johor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan, Putrajaya closed tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Schools in Johor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan and Putrajaya will be closed tomorrow due to the haze, said Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek.
In a notice posted on social media, Fadhlina said the closure on Oct 13 would also cover schools under the Hulu Langat, Petaling Perdana, Kuala Langat and Sepang District Education Offices (PPD) in Selangor, as well as the Kuantan and Rompin PPDs in Pahang.
"Schools in Kuala Lumpur, Labuan, Kedah, Kelantan, Perlis, Penang, Perak, Terengganu, Sabah and Sarawak will operate as usual," she said.
Schools in other districts in Selangor and Pahang not covered by the closure would also continue operating as usual.
"For schools operating as usual, school authorities are requested to ensure that outdoor activities are monitored according to current air quality conditions," she said.
Fadhlina also advised parents, students and school staff to wear appropriate face coverings when outdoors, particularly in areas affected by the haze.
"All parties are requested to follow official announcements from their respective school authorities, PPD and State Education Department to stay updated," she added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KLIA to conduct full-scale emergency exercise on Wednesday — MAHB
Article:
SEPANG: Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) will conduct a full-scale emergency exercise, Ex Perisai Panthera 2026, on Runway 2 on Oct 14.
Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) said in a statement today that the exercise, scheduled from 8 am to 2 pm, was part of KLIA's ongoing efforts to strengthen its emergency preparedness.
"The full-scale exercise will test response capabilities, compliance with stipulated timeframes and the effectiveness of coordination among the teams involved," it said.
MAHB said the exercise would be conducted with national security and emergency agencies as well as strategic partners, in accordance with the KUL Aerodrome Emergency Plan (KUL AEP) and international aviation safety standards.
"The exercise will involve fire engines, helicopters, simulated smoke and sirens. These activities may be visible or audible from around the Spotter Deck and Jalan Pekeliling.
"All movements and activities have been planned and controlled as part of the exercise, and the public is advised not to be alarmed," MAHB said, adding that flight operations at KLIA Terminals 1 and 2 were expected to proceed as usual.
It said any developments concerning airport operations would be communicated through KLIA's official social media channels. — BERNAMA
